messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for router-service v3.4.7 -> 5% traffic in eu-west-1. Build: sha@abc123. (deploy id: d-9876)

alice.k: seeing a small spike, digging in.

infra-bot: Alert: router-service latency p95 jumped from 80ms to 1.2s for canary group (2026-03-15T01:05Z)

ben.s: confirmed 502/503 increase in EU canary. tailing logs now.

alice.k: looks like connections aren't draining — old pods still receiving sticky sessions. health checks OK but requests routed to older variant.

carla: hmm, check feature-flag for session-affinity. I toggled it as part of rollout but maybe the flag didn't propagate to proxy layer.

ben.s: hitting instance directly: 10.20.5.12 -> header X-Instance-Variant: v3.4.6 but registry shows v3.4.7.

alice.k: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T01:04:12Z INFO connection accepted client=54.23.11.2 session_id=xyz sticky=true variant=v3.4.6
2026-03-15T01:04:13Z WARN conn-drain failed session_id=xyz reason=stuck
```

ben.s: I think flag-service didn't flip 'disable-session-affinity' for some proxies — race during config rollout.

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-20260315-423 — Canary sticky-sessions blocking drain -> elevated to P1 for canary traffic. Pager: @jordan_oncall

jordan_oncall: on it. what is customer impact?

alice.k: impact limited to ~5% of traffic in eu-west-1 canary cohort. errors 502/503 and p95 latency ~1.2s. no data loss; clients may have retried some requests.

carla: mitigation options: 1) flip flag globally (higher blast radius), 2) stop canary traffic + evict pods (safe), 3) patch flag-service and force-refresh (fast if quick).

ben.s: recommend stop canary traffic + force drain/evict. canary weight -> 0%, then evict canary pods.

jordan_oncall: agreed. execute kill-switch to remove traffic from canary. @alice.k can you set routing weight?

alice.k: doing now. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set-weight --service router-service --scope eu-west-1 --group canary --weight 0 --confirm
```

alice.k: set-weight returned OK. monitoring.

infra-bot: DeployBOT: Routing change applied for router-service in eu-west-1, canary weight=0. (op d-9876)

ben.s: traffic drop confirmed. request volume to canary -> near zero. evicting canary pods now: `kubectl drain svc/canary-router -l rollout=canary --ignore-daemonsets`

carla: watch for connection leakage — if pods still show ESTABLISHED sockets we may need SIGTERM then SIGKILL.

ben.s: drained 3/3 pods; 2 pods still with stuck sockets. sending SIGTERM.

alice.k: SIGTERM sent -> waiting 30s.

ben.s: after 30s still sockets open. force-killing.

infra-bot: Eviction completed. Canary pods terminated.

jordan_oncall: do we need a code rollback? stable is already receiving all traffic after kill-switch.

carla: root cause is flag-service propagation, not code in router-service. plan: redeploy flag-service with refresh hook, add blocking check to rollout path, and add audit for flag propagation.

alice.k: opening post-mortem ticket and adding timeline. drafting a customer-facing note: "We briefly impacted a subset of EU canary traffic; we've diverted traffic and terminated the canary rollout. No lasting customer data impact." can someone send to support?

maria_p: I'll draft and notify support & cs. low CV impact. ETA for flag-service patch? carla?

carla: patch merging now. will canary deploy flag-service patch to 1% to exercise refresh, then ramp. ETA ~25m.

ben.s: after patch we'll rerun canary with explicit flag refresh call and confirm no sticky sessions.

jordan_oncall: handing off to night oncall @oncall-next (cc @sre-bot). State: canary traffic 0, canary pods terminated, stable traffic healthy, p95 ~90ms. monitoring for 30m.

jordan_oncall: @oncall-next — takeover note: see INC-20260315-423, check flag-service rollout logs, routing weights, and proxy refresh failures. if errors reappear escalate to infra.

oncall-next: taking over. I'll watch dashboards and tail logs for residual retries. please post post-mortem link when ready.

carla: postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-987 (drafted). Root cause: race in flag propagation during feature-flag rollout sequence. Action items: 1) block canary until flags confirmed; 2) add retry+audit to flag-service; 3) add canary kill-switch runbook.

alice.k: adding logs and timeline to the ticket. closing thread after handoff unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: Note: scheduled follow-up meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC for RCA review."
